findings.comment: Add note to cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Notification is required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact information: [Austin Energy contact details]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for entire project
findings.observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) reveals the following: Sheet 1 contains project title, location map, fire department requirements, environmental notes, various compliance statements, but NO note requiring 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work begins near overhead lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 includes 'Electric Transmission Notes' (16 items) which specifically require (Item 3): 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction... OSHA requires a 20' clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' This note applies specifically to TRANSMISSION facilities and includes a 48-hour requirement for a SAFETY MEETING. However, Sheet 3, Blocks 8/14 ('Electric Notes') address general distribution lines but contain NO requirement for 48-hour notification before construction work begins near distribution overhead lines. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, requires notification to utilities before work on high-voltage lines, and UCM § 1.10.2 incorporates this requirement. The plans do not include this general notification requirement for distribution lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 explicitly requires a plan note: 'Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a 48-hour pre-construction safety MEETING for transmission lines specifically, there is NO corresponding note for general construction notification before work begins near distribution overhead lines. This is a regulatory and safety requirement distinct from the transmission-specific safety meeting. The note is required to be on the cover sheet or in the general notes to inform owner, contractor, and City of the notification requirement.

findings.comment: Specific 48-hour notification note required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 is not clearly called out on cover sheet or plans. Add conspicuous note: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work near overhead electric lines. Contact [Austin Energy contact information].'
applicableAreas: Entire site with adjacent construction
findings.observation: Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) have been reviewed. Block 14 of Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy requirements addressing maintenance of clearances per NESC and OSHA but is phrased as developer responsibility language. The specific requirement per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 for owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines is not clearly called out as a discrete note on the cover sheet or title block. Blocks 14 and 20 of Sheet 3 reference general clearance responsibilities but the explicit 48-hour notification notice with contact information is not visibly highlighted or separated as a specific callout.
findings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 Section 752.003 requires notification to Austin Energy 48 hours before work near overhead electric lines. This requirement must be conspicuously noted on site plans. While general Austin Energy notes are present on Sheet 3, the specific 48-hour notification requirement is not clearly set out as a distinct, stand-alone note with notification procedures. Best practice is to include this as a separate, highlighted note on the cover sheet with contact information for Austin Energy notification.

findings.comment: Plans do not include required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. Add this requirement to the cover sheet general notes or site plan release notes in a location where all contractors and the owner will see it during project execution.
applicableAreas: General notes on cover sheet or site plan sheets
findings.observation: The cover sheet (Sheet 1) and general notes sheet (Sheet 3) were reviewed in detail. Sheet 1 contains standard project information, Fire Department requirements, and administrative notes, but no mention of a 48-hour notification requirement to Austin Energy. Sheet 3 contains comprehensive notes about utilities, construction sequence, benchmarks, fire department requirements, and electric transmission clearances, but no explicit note requiring the owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy 48 hours before work near high-voltage overhead lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly contains site plan release notes but no mention of the 48-hour notification requirement. While Sheet 9's release notes (Block 7) reference general utility relocation responsibility (Item 4: 'The owner is responsible for all costs of relocation of, or damage to, utilities' and Item 5: 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date'), there is no specific note stating that 'owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's Documentation Requirements section explicitly states: '48-hour notification plan note: Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' The grouping further lists under Common Violation Patterns: 'Missing 48-hour notification note: Site has overhead lines and construction staging area adjacent, but no plan notes addressing notification requirement.' Since overhead electric facilities clearly exist on and adjacent to this site, and construction is planned adjacent to these lines, the required notification note must be prominently displayed on the plans.

findings.comment: Transmission facility presence and location unclear. Plans reference transmission-specific safety requirements and 25-foot clearance zones (Block 20, Sheet 3) but do not clearly identify transmission structures or establish their locations relative to grading limits. Must clarify whether transmission infrastructure exists and provide specific locations of transmission poles, structures, and guy anchors if present; otherwise, transmission-specific requirements should be removed from plans to avoid confusion during construction.
applicableAreas: Site-wide grading and construction
findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains 16 detailed notes referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, and requiring 25-foot no-dig/grade zones and Austin Energy coordination. However, vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), and Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) found no transmission poles, transmission structures, or transmission-level easements depicted. Only distribution-level infrastructure is visible: 5-foot electric easements, overhead distribution line along Valley View Road, and utility poles with guy wires. facts.md does not mention any transmission facilities. The plans do not clearly establish the presence, location, or extent of any transmission structures or transmission easement that would require the 25-foot evaluation zone and Austin Energy coordination referenced in Block 20.
findings.reasoning: Block 20 explicitly requires coordination with Austin Energy before grading within 25 feet of transmission structures and notes that grading near transmission must be coordinated with Andrew Perez (512-505-7153). The code citation UCM § 1.14.5.2 requires excavations deeper than 1 foot within 25 feet of transmission foundations to receive Austin Energy evaluation and approval. However, the plans do not clearly identify any transmission structures, their locations, or the boundaries of any transmission easement. The presence of detailed transmission notes combined with absence of transmission infrastructure depiction creates ambiguity about whether transmission facilities exist on or immediately adjacent to the property. Without confirmation of transmission structure presence and location, the applicability of this requirement cannot be determined, nor can compliance be verified. The plans must clearly establish: (1) whether transmission infrastructure exists on or within 25 feet of the property, (2) the specific locations of any transmission structures or guy anchors, and (3) the spatial relationship between grading areas and these structures.

findings.comment: Applicant must contact Andrew Perez at Austin Energy (512-505-7153) and obtain written approval for all grading and excavation within 25 feet of transmission structures and guy anchors before construction commences. Submit proof of Austin Energy's written approval of the grading plan to the Development Services Department. If grading is required within the 25-foot zone, applicant must demonstrate depth limitations and provide drainage impact analysis per UCM § 1.14.5.2.
applicableAreas: areas within 25 feet of transmission pole bases and guy anchor locations, particularly near Pole 1 (NW) and Pole 3 (SE)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors. Grading near electric transmission facilities must be coordinated with Austin Energy prior to commencement of grading. Call Andrew Perez at 512 505 7153 to schedule a meeting.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows the proposed site grading with contour lines, building foundations, retaining walls, and storm drainage throughout the site. The site map shows grading and construction activities occurring throughout the property, including areas that appear to be within 25 feet of transmission pole locations (particularly around Pole 1 at NW corner and Pole 3 at SE area based on existing conditions shown on Sheet 4). However, the plans provide NO DOCUMENTATION that Austin Energy has reviewed the grading plan, approved it, or confirmed that no excavation deeper than 1 foot will occur within 25 feet of transmission structures.
findings.reasoning: The property has transmission structures with guy anchors that require a 25-foot protection/evaluation zone per UCM § 1.14.5.2. Any grading or excavation within that zone requires prior Austin Energy coordination and approval. The plans show grading throughout the site, but do not demonstrate that applicant has obtained the required Austin Energy approval for grading within 25 feet of transmission structures. This is a mandatory procedural requirement that must be documented before site plan approval. Per UCM § 1.16.0, applicants must demonstrate compliance with transmission facility requirements; the absence of this documentation is non-compliance.

findings.comment: Grading and excavation (approximately 3 feet of cut) proposed within 25 feet of transmission structure at NW corner without documented Austin Energy coordination or approval.
applicableAreas: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly depicts a power pole (labeled 'P.P.') with guy wire (labeled 'GUY') at the NW corner of the property along Valley View Road. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows significant grading and excavation occurring immediately adjacent to and potentially within 25 feet of this transmission structure location. Specific contour analysis shows: existing grade at NW corner approximately 688-689 feet; proposed grade approximately 686.10-686.20 feet, indicating approximately 2-3 feet of excavation/cut occurring directly at the property line where the transmission pole is located. No notes on the grading plan indicate Austin Energy coordination, evaluation, or approval for this excavation.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 2) explicitly state: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors. Grading near electric transmission facilities must be coordinated with Austin Energy prior to commencement of grading.' The grading plan demonstrates that excavation is occurring at the exact location of the transmission structure (NW corner). No documentation of Austin Energy coordination or approval for this grading activity is visible on the plans. This constitutes a direct violation of the stated requirement.

findings.comment: Applicant must document that a pre-construction safety meeting has been scheduled with Austin Energy at least 48 hours before any construction commences. Contact Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule. If tower cranes will be used, include Chuck Hendry (512-505-7151). Provide proof of scheduling or meeting completion before construction begins.
applicableAreas: entire site near transmission facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) explicitly requires 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction.' The sheet provides contact information for Andrew Perez (512-505-7153) and notes that Chuck Hendry (512-505-7151) should be included if cranes are used. However, the site plan provides no documentation that this pre-construction safety meeting has been scheduled or that Austin Energy coordination has occurred. No reference in construction notes or supplementary documents confirms this mandatory coordination has taken place.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3 are explicit contractual requirements that apply to this development. The presence of transmission poles, guy wires, and transmission easements on the site (confirmed on Sheet 4 existing conditions) makes this requirement applicable. The site plan shows construction will occur in proximity to transmission structures (buildings, grading, landscaping planned throughout site). While the requirement is stated, there is no affirmative evidence in the plans or supporting documents that the applicant has actually scheduled the required 48-hour-prior meeting or obtained Austin Energy's pre-construction approval. Per the permit standard, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate compliance, not merely reference the requirement.

findings.comment: Pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy not documented as scheduled or completed. Site plan references Andrew Perez contact information but provides no evidence of meeting confirmation 48 hours before construction.
applicableAreas: Construction near transmission poles and guy wires at NW and SW corners along Valley View Road
findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 3) states: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction. Call Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule a tailgate safety meeting.' This requirement is documented on the plans. However, no evidence exists that this meeting has been scheduled, completed, or documented. Sheet 4 existing conditions survey confirms two power poles with guy wires exist at NW and SW corners on Valley View Road frontage. Construction is proposed within or immediately adjacent to these facilities (excavation visible on Sheet 11 near NW pole). No certificate or documentation of completed pre-construction safety meeting is provided in the site plan submittal.
findings.reasoning: While the site plan acknowledges the pre-construction coordination requirement by referencing the Austin Energy contact and the 48-hour notice requirement, there is no affirmative evidence that this meeting has been scheduled or completed. This is a procedural requirement that must be satisfied before construction begins. The presence of the requirement on the plans is not equivalent to compliance; completion documentation is necessary to confirm the deficiency is resolved.

findings.comment: Add a specific construction note on Sheet 3 or 6 requiring: 'Contractor shall contact One Call at 1-800-344-8377 at least 48 hours before beginning ANY excavation, trenching, or digging to locate and mark all existing underground utilities. All excavation must comply with UCM § 1.10.10.5.'
applicableAreas: any excavation or trenching areas on site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric service routing and trenching throughout the site. Sheet 3 (General Notes) includes the Texas 811 'Call Before You Dig' logo and general utility verification statements. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes utility routing notes. However, the construction notes do not explicitly state that One Call (1-800-344-8377) will be contacted before digging. The general utility notes state 'Contractor shall contact Texas 811 for assistance in determining existing utility locations prior to beginning construction' but this is not a clear, specific construction note that One Call will be contacted before work begins.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.5 requires One Call notification before digging/excavation. The site plan shows extensive trenching for utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain, electric) and grading throughout. While the general concept of utility verification is mentioned, a specific, documented commitment to contact One Call by phone (1-800-344-8377) should appear prominently in construction notes to ensure contractor compliance and documentation. The requirement is referenced but not explicitly stated as a construction sequence item.

findings.comment: One Call (1-800-344-8377) contact requirement not explicitly documented in construction notes despite significant excavation and underground electric service routing proposed.
applicableAreas: Throughout site where excavation/grading proposed
findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 13 (Fire Department requirements) and other construction notes reference standard disclaimers about utilities. Sheet 3 mentions 'Texas 811 Call Before You Dig' requirement in boilerplate but specific One Call (1-800-344-8377) contact notification is not explicitly documented in construction notes. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows excavation at NW corner with approximately 3-foot cuts proposed, but no specific construction note references One Call notification for underground electric facility verification.
findings.reasoning: While the Texas 811 logo appears on multiple sheets as a standard boilerplate element, the specific requirement to contact One Call (1-800-344-8377) before digging to locate and mark underground electric facilities is not explicitly stated in the construction notes reviewed. Given that Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing and Sheet 11 shows significant excavation/grading, specific One Call notification documentation is required but not provided in the plans.

findings.comment: Bike rack locations not dimensioned relative to transformer pads on site plan. Provide dimensioned layout showing all bike rack locations and demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance from each transformer pad.
applicableAreas: All proposed bike rack locations relative to transformer pads
findings.observation: Site plan (Sheet 9) notes that 41 bicycle parking spaces are provided (39 long-term in garages, 2 short-term). Construction details (Sheet 22) shows bike rack installation specifications including 3-foot minimum clearance from utilities. However, site plan drawings do not show specific bike rack locations in relation to transformer pad locations. Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but does not indicate bike rack locations. No dimensioned drawings provided showing bike rack positions relative to transformer pads.
findings.reasoning: Site planning convention requires minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to bike racks. While the site plan documents total bike rack count and construction standards, it does not provide dimensioned drawings showing specific bike rack locations relative to transformer pad positions. Without a bike rack layout plan with dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether laydown curbs are required without transformer locations shown on site plan and landscape plan. If transformers are located >6 feet from parking/traffic areas, identify the required access routes and verify curbing is laydown curb per UCM § 1.14.4 rather than standard curb. This item is conditional on transformer locations being visible on discipline plans.
applicableAreas: Site Plan (Sheet 9)
Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
findings.observation: The site plan shows electric easements labeled with dimensions (5' Electric Easement, 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement) and indicates easements are not within transmission easement areas based on the labeled easement types (distribution easements, not transmission). The facts.md mentions 'No Regulating Plan' applies and the site is not in a Network Area, so transmission easements are not anticipated. Transformer pads are shown on Sheet 21 but not on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, making it impossible to verify whether transformers are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces or if laydown curbs are required. Curbing on the site appears to be standard curb as shown in landscape and grading plans, not laydown curb.
findings.reasoning: Laydown curbs are required only when: (1) curbing is within transmission easement/ROW, OR (2) along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads NOT within 6 feet of drivable surface. The applicability of this item depends on: (A) whether a transmission easement exists on-site (appears not to), and (B) whether any transformer pads are >6 feet from drivable surfaces (cannot be verified from available plans). Without transformer locations on the site plan and landscape plan, distances to drivable surfaces cannot be measured. No indication is given that transformers are in transmission easement areas.

findings.comment: Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing clearance distance from proposed sidewalk alignment to existing power poles at each end of the property along Valley View Road right-of-way frontage. Confirm sidewalk clearance from pole locations, particularly at northwest and southwest property corners.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks along Valley View Road at property limits
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows utility poles along Valley View Road adjacent to the property. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a proposed '5' Concrete Sidewalk' labeled 'Construct 5' Concrete Sidewalk' in the sidewalk easement area along the western property boundary adjacent to Valley View Road. However, Sheet 9 provides NO dimension annotations showing the alignment of the proposed sidewalk relative to the existing utility poles. The sidewalk alignment appears to follow the property line, but the exact horizontal distance from poles is not dimensioned. Sheet 22 shows standard sidewalk construction details but contains no site-specific dimension relating the sidewalk to pole locations.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under Reviewer Convention is that sidewalks must be 'cleared from existing power poles at each end of property along right-of-way.' This implies that the sidewalk should not conflict with or be immediately adjacent to pole locations at property corners. Without dimension annotations showing the distance from the proposed sidewalk to existing pole locations at the northwest and southwest property corners where the property meets Valley View Road, compliance cannot be verified. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted an 'AT&T Pole' at the northwest corner, suggesting a utility pole exists at or near that location.

findings.comment: Clearly depict on site plan the location of existing down guy wire anchor points shown on the existing survey (Sheet 4). Verify that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchors or guy wire cables. If conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles per utility company standards.
applicableAreas: Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features relative to down guy wires from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a 'GUY ANCHOR' symbol (per the legend) at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road, indicating down guy wires are present on the existing utility infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site layout with driveways, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths, but does NOT depict existing guy wire locations or down guy anchor points. The survey shows the guy anchor exists, but its location relative to the proposed driveways and accessible paths is not dimensioned or verified on Sheet 9. Without down guy wire locations being shown on the site plan and without verification that proposed accessible routes, driveways, or site features do not conflict with guy anchors and cables, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.reasoning: Down guy wires are support cables from distribution utility poles to ground anchors. They represent a potential obstruction and conflict risk if proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features are routed over or through the guy anchor zone. UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) defines 'Down Guy' as a distinct feature. The grouping guidance notes that electric utility infrastructure (poles, guy wires, guys) is 'frequently omitted from plans,' suggesting this is a common deficiency. Sheet 4 confirms a guy anchor exists, but Sheet 9 does not show where it is located in relation to proposed site features. If the guy anchor conflicts with proposed improvements, the code requires either (1) pole relocation, or (2) conversion to self-supporting steel poles. The applicant has not addressed this possibility.

findings.comment: Depict on site plan and plat all down guy anchor easement boundaries for existing utility poles, showing 10-foot easement width extending minimum 5 feet past the point where the guy wire enters the ground. Verify that proposed site features (buildings, driveways, sidewalks, landscaping) do not encroach on or obstruct the down guy anchor easement area.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a guy anchor symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show easement boundaries, but facts.md indicates that critical easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show or reference down guy anchor easement boundaries. The grouping guidance specifies that down guy anchor easement requirements are: '10 feet wide extending 5 feet past where down guy enters ground' (per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards). Without easement boundaries shown on the plat or site plan, and without dimension annotations confirming the 10-foot width and 5-foot extension, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: According to Reviewer Convention and Austin Energy standards, down guy anchor points require dedicated easements to ensure access for maintenance, replacement, and inspection. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point. The existing survey (Sheet 4) confirms a guy anchor exists, but the plat (Sheet 2) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not show or reference the dedicated easement for this anchor. Without easement boundaries shown and dimensioned, applicant has not demonstrated that required easement space is provided and protected from development impacts (buildings, paving, landscaping, etc.).

findings.comment: Provide construction staging/logistics plan (or site phasing plan) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance boundaries from overhead distribution lines (marked as exclusion zones); (3) crane swing radius zones with 10-foot radial clearance from energized lines; (4) 20-foot clearance from transmission lines if transmission structures are present; (5) note requiring contractor to maintain clearances and reference to OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, material storage zones, and equipment laydown areas throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) addresses temporary erosion control measures and construction sequencing but does not include a detailed construction staging plan or equipment layout plan showing staging areas, equipment zones, crane swing radius, or material storage locations in relation to overhead electric lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site development layout but does not designate specific construction staging areas or address 10-foot radial clearances during construction. NO plans address OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2 requirements for 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines during construction activities. The sheet list shows no separate 'Construction Phasing Plan' or 'Construction Staging Plan' sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 references OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements for construction working clearances. The grouping guidance states: 'Minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) [for] construction working clearances.' This is a mandatory safety requirement during construction and is distinct from permanent clearances. Additionally, the grouping notes: 'OSHA requires a 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' The plans do not demonstrate that construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms will maintain required clearances from overhead energized lines. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide a construction staging/logistics plan addressing these safety clearances.

findings.comment: Add barricade placement details to the Erosion Control Plan (Sheets 5-7) showing 10-foot barricades erected around all transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3) and guy anchor locations before construction begins. Include this on the construction sequence diagram and reference it in construction notes.
applicableAreas: 10-foot zone around transmission poles (Pole 1 NW corner, Pole 3 SE corner) and guy anchor locations
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'Barricades must be erected 10 feet from electric transmission structures during construction.' Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) shows temporary erosion control barriers and construction sequencing. However, the plan does not show barricades specifically placed 10 feet from the three utility poles (Pole 1 at NW corner where construction occurs, and Pole 3 at SE corner) or from the guy anchor location. The erosion control plan does not delineate a 10-foot protection zone around transmission structures with specific barricade placement as required.
findings.reasoning: The transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3 with guy anchors) are located within or immediately adjacent to the construction limits (per Sheet 4 existing conditions and Sheet 9 site plan showing proposed buildings). Construction activities including grading, building construction, and utility work will occur near these structures. UCM § 1.14.9 requires barricades to be erected before construction commences. The specific placement of barricades at 10-foot distances from transmission structures is a safety and access requirement that must be shown on the construction/erosion control plans.

findings.comment: Excavation exceeding 1 foot in depth (approximately 2-3 feet) within 25 feet of transmission structure lacks Austin Energy evaluation and approval documentation.
applicableAreas: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms transmission pole and guy anchor at NW corner. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) documents excavation depths showing proposed cut of approximately 2-3 feet at the NW corner property line where the transmission structure is located. This exceeds the 1-foot depth threshold that triggers the UCM § 1.14.5.2 evaluation requirement. No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that this excavation greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of the transmission foundation has been reviewed and approved is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.5.2 states that excavations greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of transmission foundations require Austin Energy evaluation and approval. The grading plan clearly shows excavation at the NW corner of approximately 2-3 feet in depth, which exceeds the 1-foot threshold. Without documentation of Austin Energy review and approval in the site plan submittal, this deficiency cannot be resolved. The presence of excavation specifications on the plan without the corresponding approval documentation demonstrates non-compliance.

findings.comment: Guy wire anchor locations from existing conditions survey not adequately depicted on grading and site plans; 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors not established on working drawings despite proposed excavation at NW corner.
applicableAreas: NW and SW corners of property along Valley View Road where transmission structures and guy anchors located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows power poles ('P.P.') with guy wires ('GUY') and guy anchors at both the NW and SW corners of the property on Valley View Road. However, Sheets 9 (Site Plan) and 11 (Grading Plan) do not adequately depict these guy wire structures or establish 25-foot evaluation zones around them. The transmission notes require that guy anchors be treated as transmission structures for clearance purposes ('Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors'). While the poles themselves may be outside property boundaries, the guy anchors extend onto or very near the property, yet the grading plan shows excavation occurring at the NW corner with no indication of the guy anchor location or the required clearance envelope. The plans fail to show: (1) guy wire and anchor locations on grading and site plans, (2) 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors, and (3) how proposed site improvements (excavation, retaining walls) maintain clearance from guy anchors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Existing guy wire foundations and anchors' be 'shown on plans' and that 'proposed construction does not maintain required clearances from these support structures.' The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows guy wires and anchors exist at NW and SW corners. The grading and site plans do not adequately depict these structures or the 25-foot clearance zones required around them. The lack of guy anchor depiction on the working plans (Sheets 9 and 11) combined with proposed excavation at the NW corner creates uncertainty about whether clearances are maintained. Adequate depiction of guy anchors and clearance zones on all relevant working plans is required.

findings.comment: Laydown curb rated to withstand required vehicle loading not provided for Austin Energy truck access where parking areas or curbing are located along access routes to transmission easements. While COA 430S laydown curb specifications are available, the site plan does not explicitly specify where laydown curbs will be used in transmission easement areas. Clarify whether transmission easements exist on this site. If transmission easements are present along or near parking or curb areas, specify that all curbing within transmission easement access routes shall be laydown curb (over-roll curb) rated for 46,000 lb tandem axle loading with 5-foot spacing per SSM Item 430s and UCM § 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and curbing along access routes to transmission easements
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Construction Details Sheet 22 confirms that laydown curb specifications (COA 430S-1) are available and shown on the details sheet. The sheet explicitly depicts 'LAYDOWN CURB' in the curb type panel. However, vision analysis also confirms that 'There are NO transmission-specific or electrical easement-specific curb details shown on this document.' The site plan does not explicitly call out or specify which curb types will be used in areas where vehicles access transmission easements. The General Notes (Sheet 3) state that 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing)' and 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be over-roll curbing.' However, no site plan annotation indicates where transmission easements are located or whether laydown curbs are specified for those areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4.E and 1.14.4.F address transmission easement access and curb specifications. SSM Item 430s specifies laydown curb construction. The grouping's regulatory overview states 'Inadequate curb specification: Detail sheets show standard curb along transmission easement access route instead of laydown curb rated for required loading.' While the construction details sheet includes laydown curb specifications, the site plan itself does not specify whether transmission easement access routes will use laydown curbs. The applicability of this item hinges on whether transmission easements exist on this site and whether parking or curbing are located along their access routes. The extensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggest transmission facilities may be present, but the site plan layout is unclear about transmission easement locations and curb specifications. This creates ambiguity.

findings.comment: Add required callout to demolition/site plan notes: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0.
applicableAreas: Demolition plan - Sheet 8
findings.observation: Sheet 8 is titled 'Tree Removal & Demolition Plan.' The existing facility (demolished June 2022) had electric service that required removal. However, the current site plan sheets do not contain the required callout: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0. While prior demolition is complete, any future excavation or construction activities affecting underground utilities must include this coordination note.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires a specific callout on demolition/relocation plans when existing AE facilities require removal or relocation. This callout must be clearly stated on the site plan. Although prior demolition occurred, the current site plan should document that this coordination was/is required. The callout is not present on the reviewed sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) guide.md mentions that Block 2 contains 'Notes instructing coordination with the City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that 'Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated [be] clearly labeled on demolition plan'. The grouping guidance states this applies 'Only when existing electric facilities are being removed or relocated.' From facts.md and sheet reviews, the existing site was previously an assisted living facility that was demolished in 2022 (Building Permit 2022-096813 BP - Final). It is unclear from the current plans whether any existing electric infrastructure (poles, lines, transformers) from the prior structure require removal or relocation as part of the current townhome development. If they do, they must be clearly labeled on the demolition plan.

findings.comment: Identify all curbing that falls within transmission easements or along transformer equipment pad access routes, and label as 'Laydown Curb' per UCM § 1.14.4.E and Austin Energy requirements. Show curb profiles and clearance dimensions for access.
applicableAreas: grading plan
site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 states: 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be laydown curbing' and 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing).' The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows transmission easement boundaries and various curb details but does not explicitly show or label curbing as 'laydown curb' in the transmission easement areas. No drivable access routes to the transformer pads are shown, and therefore no corresponding laydown curb specifications are visible. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirms: 'Because there are no transformers depicted or located on this specific sheet, there is no visual indication or specific spot elevations demonstrating how grading directs drainage around them.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.14.4.E, laydown curbs (which provide lower profile and allow equipment access) are required when curbing is installed within transmission easements or along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces. Standard curbs impede equipment access. Sheet 3 Block 16 notes specify that grading near transmission structures must be coordinated with Austin Energy. Without showing the transformer access routes and identifying required laydown curb locations, it cannot be verified that the design accommodates Austin Energy truck access for equipment installation and maintenance.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, plans must show any required utility relocation. The demolition plan notes indicate pole/electric line removal is necessary but provides no visual coordination drawing. The development site plan should show existing poles, indicate which are to be removed or relocated, and show any new poles or routing required for the development. Without this coordination visible on the final site plan, contractors may not clearly understand the scope of electrical work required.
